key_insight: The paper shows that ultra-high-rate qLDPC codes can support fast, parallel logical operations by exploiting code symmetries and group-structured measurement schedules.
engineering_relevance: This reduces the spacetime overhead of fault-tolerant logical gates and magic-state injection, making high-rate quantum architectures more practical.
method: Partition logical qubits into symmetry-defined orbits.
Use parallel surgery to perform group-invariant Pauli-product measurements across orbits.
Apply chain-map convolution and subgroup restrictions to improve spatial and temporal overheads while controlling programmability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports concrete gadget constructions for [[256, 68, 12]], [[576, 148, 18]], and [[1152, 580, 12]] codes with about 2.5× space overhead and only 3–4 syndrome-extraction rounds.
watch_item: The programmability comes with a tradeoff: restricting to subgroups and preserving fault tolerance can reduce flexibility and may complicate hardware implementation.
paper_title: Efficient Logic with Ultra-High-Rate Quantum Codes
